questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How well you speak.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on your driving skills and behavior. You must drive safely. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Do not cause accidents or break traffic rules.

questions.question: Where is the overhead rearview mirror on a school bus?

options.text: On the right side of the bus.
On the steering wheel.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. The driver uses this mirror to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
The driver should pick up students who are walking to the bus stop.
Parents can choose where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers pick up students only at official stops set by school officials.

questions.question: If you must back up at a student pick-up point, when should you do it?

options.text: Before the students board the bus.
After the students board the bus.
While students direct you.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the students board the bus.
questions.explanation: Backing up a school bus should be avoided. If you must back up at a pick-up point, wait until all students have boarded first.

questions.question: Before evacuating a bus, what should the driver do?

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
Take time to decide if evacuation is needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher about the situation.
questions.explanation: If possible, the driver should contact the dispatcher before evacuating the bus. The decision to evacuate must be made quickly.

questions.question: With a manual transmission, what should you never do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Change gears.
Use the brakes.
Look both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your bus could stall and get stuck.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides whether to proceed?

options.text: The driver.
A traffic control device.
The vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic control device. The driver decides whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: When should you adjust the bus mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
While you are driving.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust mirrors before you begin driving.

questions.question: Why should you park at least 10 feet away from students when picking them up?

options.text: You can see their movements clearly.
You cannot get any closer to them.
Students need exercise by walking.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see their movements clearly.
questions.explanation: Park with the front bumper at least 10 feet from students. This forces students to walk to the bus, so you can watch them safely.

questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check all mirrors for students running to the bus.
Count the students and make sure all have boarded.
Allow students to board in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow students to board in pairs.
questions.explanation: Count students and check mirrors for anyone running to the bus. Students should board slowly in a single line, not in pairs.

questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces are grooved and not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle's pedals before driving. Make sure nothing is under or around the pedals. Check that the pedals work properly. The pedal surfaces should be grooved to help your foot stay in place.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must keep ____ points of contact with your vehicle at all times.

options.text: Three
Four
Two

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: When getting out of your vehicle during the driving test, face the vehicle. Always keep three points of contact with the vehicle. If you are exiting a bus, hold onto the handrail. Getting out incorrectly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: When parallel parking on the driver's side, you should:

options.text: Drive straight into the parking space.
Back past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Drive past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on the left side of your vehicle. Then back up into the space. Get the rear of your vehicle close to the back of the space. Your vehicle must be completely within the space.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check that there is enough power steering fluid.
Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, show where the power steering fluid dipstick or sight glass is. Check that the power steering fluid is at a safe level. It should not be above the full mark.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:

options.text: Form a single-file line.
Board in pairs.
Not use the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Form a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board a school bus slowly in a single-file line. For safety, they should hold the handrail while boarding.

questions.question: If a school bus stalls on a railroad track:

options.text: Students should stay on the bus.
Students should exit and stand near the bus.
Students should exit and move far away from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should exit and move far away from the bus.
questions.explanation: If the bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone off the bus right away. Move students far away from the bus at an angle away from the tracks. This protects them from debris if a train hits the bus.

questions.question: ABS helps you to:

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery surfaces.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) stop your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces. This helps you stay in control. Drive and brake the same way with or without ABS.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: In the general area described by the examiner.
In the exact position described by the examiner.
Within three feet of the position described by the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position described by the examiner.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact spot the examiner describes. If you do not follow the instructions exactly, you may fail the test.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, you:

options.text: Will not be tested on railroad crossings.
May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
Will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route does not have a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: Except for straight line backing, you may exit your vehicle to check its position during testing up to:

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can get out and check your vehicle's position during exercises. For straight line backing, you can look one time. For other exercises, you can look two times.
